selection_scope: All seven extracted YARA regex sites in the source-pinned git_submodule_carriage_return CVE-2025-48384 rule. This is a one-rule vertical slice, not a ranked top-15 sample of the malcontent corpus.
selection_basis: The rule is explicitly tied to a documented Git security advisory. The complete regex surface of this rule is reviewed so related branches and composition guards remain visible.

sites.name: path_embedded_cr
sites.reason: The terminal [^\n] class is an independently meaningful CRLF exclusion on an untrusted .gitmodules path value; the exact full-rule gate also checks composition and a real-engine mutation.

sites.name: url_embedded_cr
sites.reason: Same embedded-CR rule shape for the URL field; no separate question is counted in this one-rule slice.

sites.name: path_eof_cr
sites.reason: The anchored search mirror returned unknown in the exploratory suffix query; no UNSAT or SAT product claim is counted.

sites.name: url_eof_cr
sites.reason: Sibling of the unresolved anchored path branch; exact YARA-X behavior is covered only by the full-rule fixtures.

sites.name: path_trailing_cr
sites.reason: This regex also matches an ordinary CRLF path line; the rule requires the separate $bare_lf guard. The full YARA-X gate checks that composition.

sites.name: url_trailing_cr
sites.reason: Same condition composition as path_trailing_cr; no second property is counted.

sites.name: bare_lf
sites.reason: The source uses this marker to distinguish mixed terminators from uniform CRLF. The anchored/search composition was not proven by Z3, so the exact-engine gate is the evidence here.
